proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity covers only breach of this Agreement; as the party supplying the Interface and hosting our applicant data, TrueLink should also indemnify us for third-party IP infringement claims, breaches of law, unauthorised disclosure of Client data and its own gross negligence or wilful misconduct. We can accept the usual exclusions (Client modifications, combinations, Client specifications) if helpful.

ops.oldText: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.

rationale: Section 2(d) confirms only TrueLink's ownership; nothing confirms that Client owns its borrower/applicant data or the work product of the Support Services, while the TrueLink Intellectual Property definition sweeps in everything "associated with the Interface" (including customizations we pay for) and Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a worldwide right to resell and exploit our borrowers' Credit Data. We added a Client data/work-product ownership sentence with a licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP and a no-joint-ownership statement; TrueLink keeps the Interface.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The cap currently protects TrueLink only and applies to selected sections; our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with a mutual exclusion of consequential damages. Indemnification, confidentiality/data-security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Client's payment obligations are not capped damages.

ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID OR PAYABLE FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD AND (B) USD 1,000,000, AND NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS; CLIENT'S OBLIGATION TO PAY AMOUNTS DUE HEREUNDER SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual, remove the section-specific limitation, add floor and standard carve-outs

quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
rationale: The only cap is one-way: it protects TrueLink alone (Client's liability, including under its broad Section 12(a) indemnity, is unlimited) and it applies only to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 rather than the whole agreement. There is no USD floor, no mutual exclusion of consequential damages, no carve-out for confidentiality/data-security or indemnification, and no confirmation that Client's payment obligations sit outside the cap. We made the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with the standard Excluded Claims.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must be able to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and consent to other assignments should not be unreasonably withheld; TrueLink should not assign to a Client competitor.

ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in the case of Client, to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or equity. TrueLink shall not assign this Agreement to a competitor of Client, and no change of control of Client shall give TrueLink any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Client and a reasonableness standard on consent

quote: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Assignment is mutual and has an affiliate carve-out, but there is no M&A/successor carve-out for Client and consent is unqualified (TrueLink could withhold it arbitrarily on a sale of our business). We added the successor carve-out, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, a bar on assignment to a Client competitor, and confirmation that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to source every credit report from TrueLink without an exit. We have narrowed this to borrowers underwritten through the Interface and added the right to use other providers where TrueLink cannot deliver or fails to meet the Section 3 service levels.

ops.newText: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order from TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface; provided that Client shall be free to obtain credit reports and similar services from any third party for any other purpose, and this obligation shall not apply if TrueLink fails to meet the service levels set forth in Section 3 or the requested data is not available through the Interface.
ops.oldText: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.

proposal.summary: Add a performance-based exit to the obligation to order every credit report from TrueLink

quote: Subject to the foregoing, Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface.
rationale: The licence itself is non-exclusive, but Section 3(i) obliges Client to source a credit report from TrueLink for every borrower underwritten through the Interface, with no performance-based exit — effectively a sole-source requirement for the term (1 year, auto-renewing). We narrowed it to Interface transactions and added an exit where TrueLink misses the Section 3 service levels or cannot supply the data.

quote: Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty interest, stipulated penalties or termination charges are payable by Client — the anti-spam covenant in Section 7 and the enforcement right in Section 8(f) carry no monetary penalty, and there is no early-termination fee. The monthly minimum fees are addressed separately under MINCOMMIT. No redline.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The licence must cover our affiliates and the contractors and correspondent brokers acting on our behalf (as contemplated by the recitals) and must transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction; it should be terminable only in accordance with this Agreement, not at TrueLink's discretion.

ops.oldText: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to Client affiliates and contractors and make it transferable to a successor

quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
rationale: The grant runs to Client only — affiliates and the correspondent brokers/contractors contemplated by the recitals are not covered (and Section 8(c) limits access to Client's own officers, employees and agents), there is no successor transferability, and Section 13 terminates the licence "promptly" on certain Client breaches with no cure period. We extended the grant to affiliates and contractors, added successor transfer, and limited revocation to termination under the Agreement.

quote: Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Client — Section 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to build or buy competing software. However, Section 8(d) makes the Credit Data licence "subject to the limitations set forth in and in accordance with the Non-Competition Agreement", an instrument not defined or attached here; we should review that agreement to confirm it imposes no restraint on Client's business before signing off. No redline to this document.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept Client's existing right to terminate on notice, but it should run on 30 days' notice and be free of penalty, with any prepaid fees refunded pro rata for the period after termination.

ops.newText: until the effective date of termination specified in a written notice of Client's election to terminate this Agreement for convenience, which Client may give at any time on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice and without penalty or early-termination charge, and TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.
ops.oldText: until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Confirm 30 days' notice for Client convenience termination and add pro-rata refund of prepaid fees

quote: TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Client does have a convenience exit (service continues to the end of the following month, i.e. 30–60 days) and TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right, so we are within our fallback. It falls short of the preferred position because the notice period is indeterminate (up to two months) and there is no refund of prepaid fees; we set 30 days' notice without penalty and added a pro-rata refund.

quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
rationale: There is no audit, inspection or usage-verification right running against Client; the only information rights run in our favour (supporting documentation for charges) and the access reference in Section 9 is limited to letting TrueLink make its own Y2K repairs. Preferred position met, no redline.

quote: Any and all disputes between the parties that cannot be settled by mutual agreement shall be resolved solely and exclusively in the state or federal courts located within San Luis Obispo County, California, and each party consents to the jurisdiction of such courts and irrevocably waives any objections thereto
rationale: California law with exclusive jurisdiction of California state and federal courts, and no arbitration, falls within our accepted fallback list. The only comment is venue in TrueLink's home county (San Luis Obispo) rather than a neutral or Client-side venue such as Orange County; we would raise that as a trade only if other points are conceded, so no redline here.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The only most-favoured-nation undertaking runs in our favour (TrueLink's Hosting Services rates may not exceed those charged to any other party). No MFN obligation burdens Client, so no redline; we keep this clause as drafted.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not take minimum commitments without an exit. The monthly minimums should apply only during the current 12-month term, be reducible on 30 days' notice, and cease on termination as a true-up rather than a penalty.

rationale: Section 5(a) imposes monthly minimum fees regardless of usage, and Section 6 removes any right to contest them, on a term that renews automatically for successive years — a take-or-pay with no reduction mechanism. proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 12-month renewal term and 30-day non-renewal window work for us; we have added a cap on renewal price increases (lesser of CPI and 3%) and a 60-day renewal reminder so the opt-out is meaningful.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] On exit we need our data back and help migrating: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Client data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Client Content, Client data and borrower and loan applicant data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert post-termination transition assistance, data return and deletion certification

quote: If Client decides to discontinue Hosting Service, Client is responsible for arranging for a new hosting environment within 60 days.
rationale: Exit is handled only by placing the migration burden on Client (new name server in 30 days, new hosting environment in 60 days); there is no transition-assistance obligation, no return of our data in a usable format and no deletion certification, despite TrueLink holding the Web Site, borrower data and daily backups. We inserted the standard transition/data-return paragraph in the termination section.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's only warranty today is Y2K readiness, and the disclaimer leaves us without any conformance warranty. We have added a professional-services warranty and a 90-day conformance warranty with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund as the remedy.

ops.text: TrueLink further warrants that (a) the Hosting Services and Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Interface and each deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation; (c) it will comply with applicable law in performing hereunder; and (d) the Interface and any deliverable will be free of viruses, worms, Trojan horses and other malicious code. Client's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at TrueLink's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming services or deliverable. The express warranties in this Section are not limited or excluded by any disclaimer in this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add a TrueLink performance/conformance warranty with a real remedy and carve it out of the disclaimer

quote: EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, TRUELINK DISCLAIMS ANY AND ALL EXPENSES WARRANTIES, WARRANTIES OF FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FOR ANY MATTER RELATING TO THE ACCURACY OR COMPLETENESS, OR TIMING OF TRANSMISSION OF ANY DATA SUBMITTED THROUGH THE INTERFACE OR TO OR FROM THE WEB SITE.
rationale: TrueLink's only express warranty is Y2K date handling (Section 9); the Hosting and Support Services carry no conformance warranty, no compliance-with-law or malicious-code warranty and no remedy, while Section 3 obligations are "reasonable commercial efforts" and Section 12 disclaims the implied warranties. We inserted a workmanlike-performance and 90-day conformance warranty with repair/re-perform/refund, expressly carved out of the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink hosts our web site and handles borrower credit data, so standard cover is required: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M and cyber/privacy USD 5M, with certificates on request.

ops.text: 31. INSURANCE. TrueLink shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by law. TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

quote: 30. FORCE MAJEURE. TrueLink will be excused from delays in performing or from failing to perform its obligations under this Agreement to the extent the delays or failures result from causes beyond the reasonable control or TrueLink.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance provision at all, even though TrueLink hosts our web site and processes borrower credit data. We inserted a short insurance section (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation) with certificates on request; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback.
